raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Addresses #42548. DeepSeek V4 sizes its paged SWA host pool from the small device SWA pool using the same `--hicache-ratio` as full KV. Under long-lived prefix workloads, SWA host windows can be evicted while their full KV still fits on host, so the SWA match validator rejects the prefix and it is recomputed.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `--hicache-swa-ratio` to size only the DeepSeek V4 paged SWA host pool. Unset preserves current behavior. For example, `--hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-swa-ratio 4` doubles SWA host capacity while leaving full KV and C128 at ratio 2.
- Reject invalid or zero-page ratios and layouts without a paged SWA host pool. Require explicit `--hicache-ratio` with the override because automatic host-memory sizing assumes one shared ratio.
- Add focused registered CPU tests for argument validation, page sizing, and the unsupported layout; document the flag and per-rank RAM impact.

This is an opt-in capacity control, not a change to SWA eviction policy. A finite host pool cannot guarantee that every idle prefix survives arbitrary churn. Operators should check startup allocation lines and available host RAM per rank.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward, kernel, or sampling computation changes. The new flag changes only host-cache capacity. No model-scale accuracy replay was run; the available A10 cannot serve the issue's DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash MXFP4 configuration.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No model-scale speed benchmark or reporter-workload replay was run. The expected benefit is avoiding recomputation when SWA host pressure causes otherwise host-backed prefixes to miss; no performance claim is made without that measurement.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files`, `git diff --check`, and Python compilation passed.
- Dependency-free execution of the changed sizing and argument-resolution functions passed for default, override, invalid, implicit-ratio, and zero-page cases.
- Registered CPU tests were added but did not execute locally. I installed the required Python packages into a temporary environment on the available A10; collection then stopped while loading the pinned `sglang-kernel` wheel, which exposes SM100/CUDA 13 binaries rather than this host's SM86/CUDA 12.8 environment. Upstream CPU CI remains necessary.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused registered unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [ ] Run registered tests in upstream CI (awaiting `run-ci` from an authorized maintainer).
- [ ] Provide model-scale accuracy/speed results (not available on the current hardware; see sections above).
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

## Related work

#42443 adds an analogous Mamba host-pool control and per-pool metrics. This PR is limited to DeepSeek V4 SWA sizing and does not duplicate those metrics.

 HiCache extends RadixAttention with a hierarchy of KV cache tiers, significantly expanding effective context capacity for long-context and multi-turn scenarios.
 
 To enable HiCache, open the **HiCache** card in the [Playground above](#playground) and flip **Enable**: the Playground emits `--enable-hierarchical-cache` on top of the recipe's flags, and cold KV pages spill to CPU pinned memory (L2, GPU + CPU) instead of being dropped from the GPU pool. The host pool is sized by ratio (`--hicache-ratio 2`), not by a fixed `--hicache-size`.
+If SWA host windows are evicted while full KV remains on host, add `--hicache-swa-ratio` to increase only the SWA host pool (for example, `--hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-swa-ratio 4`). The extra host memory is allocated per rank; check startup allocation lines against available RAM.
 
 The Write policy knob controls the GPU → CPU write and defaults to `write_through` (the upstream default): every page is mirrored to the CPU tier as it is written. `write_through_selective` backs up only hot data and `write_back` defers the copy to eviction, trading cache freshness for host-side I/O.
